mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI engine replacement typically costs £3,000-£7,000 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, depending on generation and engine code (CDL, CJXC, CJXB, CYFB, DSFF, DNFF, DNFG). Used engines start from £1,200-£4,000. Fitting adds approximately £1,040-£1,560 in labour (16-24 hours at independent specialist rates). Main dealer fitted prices are typically 30-50% higher.

mainEntity.name: Does the Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EA888 2.0 TSI engine uses a timing chain, not a belt. The timing chain tensioner is a known weak point on earlier EA888 engines (Gen 1 and Gen 2). On Gen 3 and Gen 4 engines, the tensioner design was improved, but chain stretch and tensioner wear can still occur at higher mileages (100,000+ miles). Symptoms of tensioner failure include rattling on cold start.

mainEntity.name: Is the Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EA888 is a generally robust engine, but it has well-documented issues. The most common problem across all generations is water pump failure. Other issues include timing chain tensioner wear (particularly on earlier engines), carbon buildup on intake valves, and PCV system failure. With regular maintenance and preventative replacement of known weak points, the EA888 can be a reliable performance engine.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Mk7 and Mk8 Golf R engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mk7 Golf R (2013-2017) uses the EA888 Gen 3 engine producing 300hp and 380Nm. The Mk7.5 Golf R (2017-2020) produces 310hp and 400Nm. The Mk8 Golf R (2020-present) uses the EA888 Evo4 (Gen 4) producing 320-333hp and 420Nm. The Mk8 engine features a new turbocharger, higher compression, and improved efficiency.

mainEntity.name: Why does my Golf R use so much oil?

acceptedAnswer.text: Excessive oil consumption is reported on some EA888 engines. On Gen 1 engines, some owners reported burning approximately a litre of oil every 600 miles. The issue can be caused by piston ring wear, valve stem seals, or PCV system failure. If your Golf R is using more than 1 litre of oil between services, have it inspected.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen Golf R?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Mk6 Golf R (2009-2013) worth £8,000-£14,000, a rebuilt engine at £3,000-£5,000 plus fitting may represent 30-50% of the vehicle's value. For Mk7 Golf R models (£10,000-£18,000), a rebuilt engine at £3,500-£6,000 plus fitting may represent 25-40% of the vehicle's value. For Mk8 Golf R models (£25,000-£45,000), replacement is almost always worthwhile.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI 4Motion - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI 4Motion is the flagship performance variant of the Golf range, powered by Volkswagen's EA888 turbocharged 2.0-litre four-cylinder engine. The Golf R nameplate replaced the earlier Golf R32, marking a shift from the naturally aspirated VR6 to a turbocharged four-cylinder with all-wheel drive. Over three generations - Mk6, Mk7/Mk7.5 and Mk8 - the Golf R's EA888 engine has evolved from 270hp to over 330hp, with each iteration bringing improved performance, efficiency and durability.

milestones.description: Mk6 Golf R launched with EA888 Gen 2 2.0 TSI (CDL, 270hp / 350Nm)
Mk7 Golf R introduced with EA888 Gen 3 2.0 TSI (CJXC / CJXB, 300hp / 380Nm)
Mk7.5 Golf R facelift with updated EA888 Gen 3 (CYFB, 310hp / 400Nm)
Mk8 Golf R launched with EA888 Gen 4 / Evo4 2.0 TSI (DSFF, 320hp / 420Nm)
Mk8 Golf R 20 Years edition with EA888 Evo4 (DNFF, 333hp / 420Nm)

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI 4Motion Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI (EA888) is a high-performance turbocharged engine that delivers exceptional power and driving dynamics. However, like any performance engine, it has well-documented weak points. Water pump failure is the single most common issue across all generations of the EA888 in the Golf R, with leaks often developing as early as 40,000 miles. Timing chain tensioner wear, carbon buildup on intake valves, and PCV system failures are also reported. Rebuilt Golf R 2.0 TSI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Water Pump & Thermostat Housing Failure - The EA888's Most Common Weakness
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI (EA888 Gen 2 / Gen 3 / Gen 4, 2009-present)
problems.rootCause: The water pump assembly on the EA888 engine is prone to leaking. The plastic impeller can come loose from the shaft, causing the water pump to fail completely and the engine to overheat. On Gen 3 engines, the water pump is belt-driven off the balance shaft. Some owners report pump/thermostat failure at around 40,000 miles, with overheating and limp mode activation. It's fairly common to have more than one failure of this part during the lifetime of your vehicle.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat, belt; coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: If coolant leak is detected early

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace with upgraded pump with metal impeller
repairOptions.longevity: If replacing, consider upgraded unit for longevity
When overheating has caused head gasket or bottom-end damage

problems.recommendation: For Golf R owners, preventative maintenance is essential. Replace the water pump at the first sign of coolant loss - the upgraded metal impeller option offers better longevity. Listen for timing chain rattle on cold starts - if present, have the tensioner inspected immediately. Regular carbon cleaning (walnut blasting) every 50,000-80,000 miles will restore performance. If water pump failure has caused overheating or timing chain failure has occurred, a replacement engine with upgraded components and warranty often represents better long-term value than chasing individual repairs.

problems.h4: Timing Chain & Tensioner Issues - A Known EA888 Weak Point
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI (EA888 Gen 2 / Gen 3, 2009-2020)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can fail, causing the chain to become loose and potentially skip a tooth or break. Symptoms include rattling or clanking noise on startup, fault codes for incorrect timing, or excessive cranking to start. Chains and tensioners generally last approximately 100,000-150,000 miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner only - if caught very early

If water pump failure has caused overheating or timing chain failure has occurred, a replacement engine with upgraded components and warranty often represents better long-term value than chasing individual repairs.

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - Direct Injection Side Effect
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Golf R 2.0 TSI (all EA888 generations, 2009-present)
problems.rootCause: The EA888 uses direct fuel injection, meaning fuel is injected directly into the cylinder rather than across the intake valves. This means detergents in the fuel never clean the intake valves, allowing carbon to build up over time. Carbon buildup reduces airflow and hurts performance.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting to remove carbon from intake valves
